counters.note: The general-purpose counter for small things: fruit, eggs, balls. When in doubt, 個 is often acceptable.
Pencils, bottles, umbrellas, bananas, trees. The reading shifts between ほん, ぼん and ぽん.
Paper, tickets, plates, banknotes, and also shirts. Completely regular readings.
1 and 2 use native readings: ひとり, ふたり. Watch out for 4: よにん. Above ten the native readings disappear: 11人 is じゅういちにん.
The native Japanese numbers. They work for most things that are not people or animals, but only up to ten, and 10 is just とお.
Books, magazines, notebooks, dictionaries. Not 本, even though 本 means “book”!
Cars, bicycles, computers, TVs, cameras, pianos. Completely regular readings.
Cats, dogs, fish, frogs, insects. The reading shifts between ひき, びき and ぴき.
Drinks in cups or glasses, bowls of ramen or rice. Oddly, squid and crabs are counted with 杯 too. The reading shifts between はい, ばい and ぱい.
Prices. Regular except 4円, which is よえん.
Hours on the clock. Three to remember: よじ, しちじ, くじ.
Minutes. Switches between ふん and ぷん: いっぷん, さんぷん, よんぷん, ろっぷん, はっぷん, じゅっぷん.
The 1st to the 10th use native readings (ついたち, ふつか, みっか…). After that it is regular 〜にち, except 14日 じゅうよっか, 20日 はつか and 24日 にじゅうよっか. (一日 read いちにち means “one day”, a length of time: that is 日間.)
January to December are just numbers plus がつ. Three to remember: しがつ, しちがつ, くがつ.
Ages. いっさい, はっさい, じゅっさい, and the special はたち for 20.
How many times something happens: いっかい, ろっかい, はっかい, じゅっかい.
Like 回, but the 3rd floor is usually さんがい.
Cows, horses, elephants, lions, whales: animals bigger than a person.
Birds. Rabbits are traditionally counted with 羽 too, though 匹 is just as common for them today.
Shoes, socks, boots: one 足 is one pair.
Dresses, suits, coats, kimono: clothes worn on the body. Shirts can take 着 or 枚.
Canned food and drinks. Canned drinks are also often counted with 本.
Servings that come on a plate: curry, pasta, salad. 1 and 2 are ひとさら, ふたさら.
A piece cut from something bigger: a slice of pizza, cake, watermelon, meat or fish (a whole pizza is 枚, a whole cake 個). 1 and 2 are ひときれ, ふたきれ.
Bags and the things sold in them. 1 and 2 are ひとふくろ, ふたふくろ.
Boxes and things sold by the box. 1 and 2 are ひとはこ, ふたはこ; then さんぱこ, ろっぱこ, はっぱこ, じゅっぱこ.

counters.category: pairs of chopsticks, bowls of rice
counters.note: Pairs of chopsticks, and rice served in a bowl as part of a meal (杯 also works for the bowlful). Regular readings.
Pills, candies, grapes, grains of rice, raindrops. 1 and 2 are ひとつぶ, ふたつぶ.
Whole, uncut round produce: melons, onions, heads of cabbage or lettuce. Once it is cut, a piece is a 切れ. 1 and 2 are ひとたま, ふたたま.
Food on a stick: dango, oden, yakitori. 本 works too. 1 and 2 are ひとくし, ふたくし.
Pieces of nigiri sushi: in everyday use one 貫 is one piece, though some shops count a pair as one. Same readings as 缶.
Bouquets, bunches of greens, bundles of paper. 1 and 2 are ひとたば, ふたたば.
Years. 4年 is よねん.
How many months something lasts: いっかげつ, ろっかげつ, はっかげつ, じゅっかげつ.
Weeks: いっしゅうかん, はっしゅうかん, じゅっしゅうかん.
How many days something lasts: the date readings plus かん (ふつかかん, みっかかん… はつかかん). One day is usually just 一日, read いちにち, never ついたち.
Hours of time. Follows 時: よじかん, くじかん.
Nights at a hotel: いっぱく, さんぱく, ろっぱく, はっぱく, じゅっぱく.
Number one, number two: platform numbers, turns, rankings. Regular readings.
Houses, shops, restaurants. 3 is usually さんげん.
Apartment blocks, office buildings, factories. Same readings as 頭.
Planes, helicopters, rockets: いっき, ろっき, はっき, じゅっき.
Carriages of a train: one 両 is one carriage, not a whole train. Regular readings.
Ships and larger boats: いっせき, はっせき, じゅっせき. The line between 隻 and 艘 is loose; size is only a rule of thumb.
Small boats: yachts, rowing boats, canoes. 隻 is also heard for these.
Chairs, and desks or tables with legs: いっきゃく, ろっきゃく, はっきゃく, じゅっきゃく.
Letters, emails, documents sent to someone: いっつう, はっつう, じゅっつう.
Copies of newspapers, pamphlets, handouts. Regular readings.
Incidents, orders, messages, reservations: things that are handled one case at a time. Same readings as 軒, except さんけん.

counters.category: items of goods, works of art
counters.note: Items in a shop or collection, and works of art: いってん, はってん, じゅってん.
Songs and pieces of music: いっきょく, ろっきょく, はっきょく, じゅっきょく.
Questions on a test or quiz. Regular readings.
Single flowers (本 also works), and wheels. Regular readings.
Things that come as a set or a pair: gloves, a deck of cards, a couple. 1 and 2 are ひとくみ, ふたくみ.
Human-shaped things: dolls, statues, robots, snowmen: いったい, はったい, じゅったい.
Fireworks, gunshots, punches: いっぱつ, さんぱつ, ろっぱつ, はっぱつ, じゅっぱつ.
Drops of water, medicine, blood: いってき, はってき, じゅってき.
A polite way to count people, used by staff: 何名様ですか. Unlike 人, it is completely regular: いちめい, にめい.
